items.problem: The migration dropped the UWP <Application RequestedTheme="Dark"> declaration, so the WinUI 3 app renders in the system/light theme (white client) while the UWP golden is dark — a visual-parity regression. The skill's theme-migration guidance covers per-brush key remaps (ApplicationPageBackgroundThemeBrush → SolidBackgroundFillColorBaseBrush) and DynamicResource→ThemeResource, but never mentions carrying over the app-level RequestedTheme, so the agent didn't preserve it.
items.evidence: UWP source App.xaml: '<Application ... RequestedTheme="Dark">' (uwp-samples-standalone/Samples/Unicode/cs App.xaml). Migrated App.xaml (trial 000 MyWinUIApp/App.xaml) has no RequestedTheme. Golden screenshot parity/baseline/screenshots/01_*.png is dark; candidate parity/winui3/screenshots/01_*.png client is white.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md L850-852 (theme-brush key remaps / 'Some UWP theme-brush keys were removed entirely') and the DynamicResource→ThemeResource resource section.
items.why_missed: under-emphasized — the existing theme section is entirely about individual brush keys; the app-level RequestedTheme attribute on <Application> is a different, easy-to-drop knob that is never called out, so a scan of the theme guidance doesn't surface it.
items.proposed_improvement: Add a short, explicit note (one subsection + a pointer from the existing theme-brush paragraph) that <Application RequestedTheme="..."> must be carried from the UWP App.xaml to the WinUI App.xaml, because many UWP SDK samples set RequestedTheme="Dark" and dropping it silently flips the app to the system/light theme and breaks parity with the golden.
items.generalizes: RequestedTheme="Dark" (or "Light") on <Application> is a common UWP SDK-sample idiom; App.xaml is rewritten in essentially every migration, so this exact attribute is at risk of being dropped in any scenario whose original pins a non-system theme.
